title: Networking & streaming overhead: HTTP vs gRPC, chunking, proxies, backpressure
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the investigation notes and raw results from microbenchmarks we ran to quantify networking/streaming overheads for the serving runtime. Focus areas: HTTP chunked vs gRPC streaming, chunk size tradeoffs, impact of proxies (envoy/nginx) and backpressure behavior under many concurrent streams.

Background / motivation:
- We see customer reports where tail latency spikes at low qps when using client-side streaming over HTTP (chunked) behind proxies.
- Hypothesis: transport + proxy buffering + chunking policy add non-trivial per-chunk latency and backpressure interactions that increase p95.
- Goal: provide actionable knobs (chunk size, keepalive, proxy config, gRPC vs HTTP) and quantify cost/latency tradeoffs for default runtime config.

Testbed (lab):
- Serving node: 1x A100 40GB, 32 vCPU, 192GB RAM, Ubuntu 22.04. Running runtime binary built from main@2025-08-30.
- Client machine: 16 vCPU, 64GB RAM.
- Proxy box (when used): 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM running envoy 1.26 / nginx 1.25 in separate runs.
- Network: 10GbE, full-duplex, single AZ.
- Model: small synthetic LLM endpoint (decoder-only) that streams tokens as they are generated. Token generation timing simulated to mirror real model (avg token compute = 6ms on this hardware).
- Workloads: single-stream long-run (1 client, 512 token response), many-small-streams (500 concurrent short responses, 8 tokens each), steady qps runs (50/200/500 qps).

Methodology:
- For streaming we tested two transports: HTTP/1.1 chunked responses (via SDK POST + transfer-encoding: chunked) and gRPC bidi-streaming.
- Chunk sizes tested: 1 token/chunk, 4 tokens/chunk, 16 tokens/chunk, "batched full-response" (send at end).
- Proxy variants: none (direct), envoy (default config), nginx (proxy_buffering off/on).
- Measured metrics: per-request p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end), per-chunk RTT, additional CPU on proxy, observed head-of-line blocking (number of delayed streams), and throughput (tokens/s).
- Each experiment ran for 5 minutes after 30s warmup; repeated 3 times and median reported unless noted.

Key results (high-level summary):
- gRPC streaming consistently had lower p95 than HTTP chunked when chunking small (1-4 tokens). Example: single-stream 512 tokens: gRPC p50=3200ms, p95=4100ms; HTTP chunked(1 token) p50=3250ms, p95=4900ms (proxy=NONE). The delta grows with proxies.
- Chunk size tradeoff: increasing chunk size reduces total per-token latency due to fewer syscall/transfer overheads, but increases perceived latency for early tokens (first-byte). 16-token chunks hit a good compromise for latency & efficiency.
- Proxies add a non-negligible fixed overhead and can amplify tail latency under many concurrent small streams. Envoy (default) added ~8-12ms median per-chunk and amplified p95 by ~15-25% for small-chunk workloads; nginx with proxy_buffering on introduced buffering delays (saw queues and full-response buffering).
- Backpressure behavior: with many concurrent small streams (500 concurrent 8-token responses) HTTP chunked + envoy showed head-of-line behaviour where a few streams stalled for ~200-600ms due to upstream write-blocking and proxy internal buffering. gRPC showed better pipelining and fewer stalled streams, but still hit throughput limits when client write windows saturated.

Representative numbers (single-stream, no proxy, per-request latencies):
- gRPC streaming (1 token emitted every ~6ms by runtime): p50=3200ms, p95=4100ms, p99=4600ms, total_tokens=512
- HTTP chunked, 1-token chunks: p50=3250ms, p95=4900ms, p99=6100ms
- HTTP chunked, 4-token chunks: p50=3220ms, p95=4300ms, p99=4800ms
- HTTP chunked, 16-token chunks: p50=3300ms (slower p50 by ~100ms vs 4-token due to buffering delay), p95=3800ms

With envoy proxy between client and runtime (same hardware):
- gRPC: p50=3230ms (+30ms), p95=4300ms (+200ms)
- HTTP chunked 1-token: p50=3270ms (+20ms), p95=6100ms (+1200ms)
- Observed envoy CPU ~10-20% under heavy small-chunk loads; socket buffer pressure seen.

Many-small-streams (500 concurrent, 8-token responses):
- HTTP chunked (1-token chunks) + envoy: observed 12% of requests with >250ms stall before completion; p95 increased to 900ms.
- gRPC streams: p95 ~420ms, stall rate <1%.
- Notes: enabling HTTP/2 multiplexing at the proxy reduced stalls but did not eliminate buffering-induced delays when proxy buffer thresholds hit.

Qualitative analysis / root causes:
1) Per-chunk overhead: small chunks incur kernel + userspace + proxy per-chunk handling cost (syscall, framing, header handling for HTTP, flush behavior in libraries). This is multiplicative for 512-token responses.
2) Proxy buffering: proxies can choose to buffer small writes to optimize throughput. With buffering-on, proxies hold back small chunks until buffer thresholds or timeouts; this increases tail latency for streaming patterns.
3) Backpressure propagation gaps: when many streams are active, the proxy or client-side runtime may hit TCP write buffer limits; proxies that do naive buffering cause head-of-line blocking for other streams sharing the same connection.
4) gRPC (HTTP/2) benefits: multiplexed streams over a single connection reduce connection churn and are better at keeping per-stream flow control, which reduces stalls vs many independent HTTP/1.1 chunked connections.

Actionable recommendations (short):
- Default chunk size: set SDK/server default to 4-16 tokens/chunk (configurable per-route). 4 tokens reduces first-byte delay vs 16; 16 reduces proxy CPU. Recommend 8 as default for hosted API.
- Transport: prefer gRPC streaming for high-concurrency, low-latency streaming use cases. Offer HTTP streaming for compatibility but clearly document may need tuning.
- Proxy config: for envoy, tweak downstream/upstream buffer limits and stream idle timeouts; disable full-response buffering for streaming routes (set `buffer_enabled: false` or equivalent). For nginx ensure proxy_buffering is off for streaming endpoints.
- Backpressure: implement token bucket at edge and enforce per-connection concurrent-stream limits; expose metrics for socket write queue lengths and proxy buffer saturation.
- SDK: expose chunk-size and flush-interval knobs; add heuristics to switch from small-chunk mode to batched-chunk mode if runtime detects proxy buffering (via delayed first-byte).

Open questions / follow-ups / TODOs:
- Run same experiments across cross-region links (higher-latency networks) — we expect chunking tradeoffs to shift toward larger chunks when RTT >> per-token compute time.
- Repeat with real models (13B, 70B) and real token times to ensure similar patterns hold.
- Investigate kernel-level socket tuning (TCP_CORK, TCP_NODELAY) interactions with our runtime's flush strategy.
- Add synthetic tests that simulate random client pauses (to mimic flaky mobile networks) to see how proxies/flow-control behave.

Raw data snippets (median of 3 runs):
- direct_a100_gRPC_single_512: p50=3200ms, p95=4100ms, p99=4600ms, tokens_per_sec=160
- direct_a100_HTTP_chunk1_single_512: p50=3250ms, p95=4900ms, p99=6100ms, tokens_per_sec=155
- envoy_a100_HTTP_chunk1_single_512: p50=3270ms, p95=6100ms, tokens_per_sec=150, proxy_cpu=12%
- envoy_a100_gRPC_many_8tokens_500concurrent: p50=220ms, p95=420ms, stall_rate=0.8%
- envoy_a100_HTTP_chunk1_many_8tokens_500concurrent: p50=260ms, p95=900ms, stall_rate=12%

Notes to self / experiment logs (rough):
- 2025-09-18 14:12: started run; noticed envoy logs showing "stream reset" spikes when client qps ramped.
- 2025-09-18 15:03: toggled nginx proxy_buffering off; observed p95 drop from ~1.2s to ~420ms for small-chunk load.
- 2025-09-19: validated that increasing chunk size to 16 reduced envoys' CPU by ~30%.

Next steps (who/when):
- Aisha: add SDK knob to change chunk size + default to 8 tokens (owner: Aisha Patel) — due 2025-10-02.
- Ravi: create patch to envoy bootstrap config for streaming routes to disable response buffering and increase stream window (JIRA-7890) — due 2025-09-29.
- Marcus: run cross-region tests and post results to this doc (owner: Marcus Li) — due 2025-10-05.

References / related docs: networking-streaming-overhead-benchmarks.json, networking-streaming-http-grpc-chunking-benchmarks.json, networking-streaming-proxies-backpressure-benchmarks.json (see Drive folder).

Bottom line: streaming transport & chunking policy matter. For hosted defaults we should ship 8-token chunk default, recommend gRPC for high-concurrency paths, and update proxy bootstrap to avoid response buffering on streaming routes.
